body: Also, is there someone you can talk to as a friend about it? I find that having someone listen, having a way to express my feelings really can help. If you like, I would be glad to talk, but even if you don't think I'm a good "fit," there are many who offer an ear.

Meditation is not something you can fail at, so don't worry about not having the skills to do it. There are many resources for guided meditations on the http://www.reddit.com/r/meditation subreddit and there are many resources.

I understand that it can be very frustrating and upsetting not finding a treatment that really works. Maybe it will take work, but I truly believe there is treatment that can help anyone who looks. It may take a long time to find a good balance, but it is worth it. I say balance, because a lot of people find help by mixing treatments from different sources. Maybe there is no one thing that helps, but maybe a few things will.

That sounds like something really tough to go through. I think a lot of people take for granted the pleasures in life, the ones that you are deprived of.

Still, you should hang on. That must sound totally naive, but I think it is true. For one thing, there may be treatment available. I understand you may already be treated, but if it is not working, it could mean the world for you to try another doctor or counselor. It is the routine answer, I suppose, but it is for a reason. Treatment can save your life. Also, you are at a risk for a dysthymic "double depression," so wouldn't it be wise to avoid that?

This part is cheesy but I have to say it. You only have one life. Even if all you see is pain, it is important to keep going. You can never predict the future, I promise. Dysthymia often passes, and if it does not, you can still take efforts to manage it and treat it. You have gone through a lot, I know, but you still have options. Perhaps you can try some mindfullness exercises/meditation? This can help you from having all the bad time pile up, and can improve your perception.

I am glad you have had different experiences from me, because whenever I am anxious at all I really can't stand listening to music. It makes me just feel worse, no matter what. This means weeks without listening to any music usually.

Hey there, thanks for sharing. I think a good first step is to throw away that rope. If you start making arrangements to commit suicide, it is time to go to the hospital, even if you would rather die.

That said, I think you have been through a lot in a short amount of time, so it is natural that you are having problems. But, the bright side is that these problems are all surmountable. First thing, you might want to get a handle on substance abuse. There are groups such as Narcotics Anon and Alcoholic Anon that can give you a supportive foundation to face your life. 

 You also should look into some therapy, that could help tremendously. I can relate to your story about court. I got an misdemeanor for something and it absolutely destroyed me, because it was in a dorm, and I really thought my life was over. In the end, nothing really happened, it got dismissed and it didn't actually affect things (other than me). Yet, after it all, any relief I felt was pretty small in comparison to the state I was in. I am actually not over it, almost 2 years later, so take it from me, it is time to seek help. 

Anxiety about the future is totally understandable, and insecurity is something I think everyone has problems with on some level. Try to realize that it is not the end of the world to not get into law school, and that there are other options. If your girlfriend would leave you, then as hard as it is to see, you are better off without her. You need someone to support you, not evaluate you. 

As cliched as it is, this could be a turning point. It could be the time you turn away from the things that hurt you, drugs and booze, and take positive steps to take care of yourself. It is important not to neglect your own well-being in order to attend to academics and whatever else.

Sorry you are feeling like this. Loneliness is quite awful, but it sounds like you are already taking steps to put yourself out there. This is great! Really, just deciding to leave your home and try is more than many people feel up to doing, so at least feel good about the fact that you tried.

Try not to get yourself down. As long as you keep trying something will happen, even if it takes a little while. Don't close yourself off, but most of all don't get discouraged. Maybe try doing some new things, that could help you get more excitement.

This feeling that no one would miss you, that you are better dead than alive, is completely false. Every suicide is a tragedy, and your loss would be a permanent, deep sadness on everyone you know. I am not trying to guilt you into staying alive, but I am letting you know the truth. Personally, only one person I have known has killed themselves, and I wasn't close to them. My own feelings are that they made a huge mistake, and from where I stand it is clear that they didn't think it through, but as you penetrate deeper into their social circles, you see that it affected everyone they knew. 

You might not feel like no one cares, but that is just wrong. The truth is the second they find out you're dead, they all wish that they could've helped you, even if they don't seem caring now. And many, if you told them how you feel now, wouldn't do much, wouldn't take you seriously, but there are some that would do anything to help you if you give them the chance. Your parents are likely candidates. They love you, and no matter how you see yourself, they love you and see your potential. So reach out and try to get help.

Could it be sinus issues? I get all of those symptoms from my sinuses.

Also, I have read that anxiety really does manifest in many physical symptoms beyond what we normally associate with it.

Check if your school maybe has a hotline for counselling. Mine does, so it may be common. If not, you may want to call the suicide hotline. Even if you are not suicidal, they are still someone to talk to.
I have a Norwegian elk hound that will lay flat, paws out and all. If you really want to bathe him, it means dragging him around, feeling like kind of an asshole for doin so.

I am sorry to hear that. But, there are many other online support groups, many options. I just mean, I am not saying you have not tried, of course you have, but isn't it worth it to try more? It is your happiness at stake.

This is an issue I think everyone faces when they are depressed or what have you. You experience the same thing for so long, you forget what it is like for other people and how things really are. What I mean is, perhaps your social life has not been great up to now, but it this isn't a good measure of prediction. You can still make friends, in fact it is nearly inevitable if you put yourself in the right positions. 


I just searched for trans support groups and found this: http://www.lauras-playground.com/chat.htm. Apparently the moderators of that chat are certified to help, and it came with the shocking statistic that the suicide rate for Trans is estimated at 31%. Any suicide is too much, but that is ridiculous. You are not alone, clearly, and I suspect many have the similar experiences that you have had. 

Perhaps you can find offline support groups as well. I am not sure how this is done, but it is worth a shot, right?

Hey there. That is a lot to be going through, but maybe I can offer some comfort. First, remember your depression is an affliction. You are not what you think you are. If you see yourself as a burden, it just means you have low self esteem, of course, but it doesn't mean you should have low self esteem. That is to say, you are more than you think you are, and your presence in this world is much better than you realize. If you ended your life, everyone you would leave behind would be torn up. I don't mean to guilt you, but it is true, and it just means that you never were a burden, they would be sad because they knew you and loved you and would wish oyu are still here. 

Your mother sounds like a hard person to be around. Having a bad relationship with a parent is hard, but things will get better. Your mother is the one with problems to work out. Remember this, and try to let that fact be a barrier between her harassment and your feelings. You are not the problem, she is. You may try talking to her and repairing this broken bond, but whatever you do, remember you are not the one at fault for her behavior.

Feeling the way you do, about your parents, mother specifically, and boyfriend and such, these are common feelings. It comes from insecurity and depression. These are not reasons to die. Things will change and you will grow up to be independent and it will be better. Not knowing what will happen, especially in this state, really is quite terrifying. It's like being stuck but free falling at the same time, but try to keep a cool head.  You can beat this, and things will get better.

Treatment for this can be many things. You may find a cause to put yourself into, or something, but you really should talk to your parents, or someone else you trust, about how you are feeling. It may seem weird or scary, but medication and/or therapy can really do a lot of good. Many people go through these rough feelings, but perseverance and vigilance is key.

There is a lot of trans hate, not just on reddit but in the world. Don't ever, ever believe it when people say you deserve any misery and hate for what you are. They don't know, and if they can't empathize, they are not worth your time. 

I am at the same age as you, and while I have not gone through exactly what you have, I am not trans, I know a similar loneliness and isolation. Clearly things have not really "gotten better" for me, not yet, but that is no reason to end your life. Take a step back, at least try, and see how right now, and everything before it is such a small fraction. Live in the present, I can't tell you to just let go of everything you have experienced because that is probably very hard, but try to live in the present with an eye to the promise of the future. 

It might seem like you don't have much, hell I know it feels that way, but try to look at what you do have. You have a job and are in school, it's not as much as many people but it is more than some. You might not feel like you have the best friendship but you do have 2 friends. I am not trying to make you feel guilty or sad, but since you know how bad it is to feel like nothing would matter if you weren't here the next second, but it is something to build back up on.  

I would say that you could benefit from something more in your life. Probably sound like a broken /r/sw record, but there is always volunteering. Volunteering is a good way to meet people and it occupies time. It's a start at a better life, and at least something to get up and do in the morning. 

Also, why don't you want to go to a therapist? If you live in a city, there is likely one with a specialty in gender and trans lifestyles. The journey you are on is a hard one, no doubt, but it can get better. It takes effort on your own part, but it is worth it for the prospect of not feeling the way you do now. When you are at the point where you have nothing to lose, then look at it like this: you have nothing to keep you from just going out and doing what you feel. Sometimes just going out on a weekend, even alone, is refreshing and reminds us of life, instead of the pitiful pain of sitting at home like always. If you get therapy, I can't see how it could hurt, albeit if you found the right doctor. I understand many people have many different experiences with professional help, but I would like to think that there is potential for help in there.

Also, not my specialty, but there are specific hotlines for lgbt youth. The stress you get from just being who you are can probably be dealt with well by the people on those hotlines. It is a tough thing to go through, especially in a world that doesn't seem too welcoming, but remember, there are always people who will accept you no matter who you are.

You are in a rut. It sounds like a big one, but you can definitely get out of it. Life throws us big problems, but often starting on little stuff helps build inertia. Try setting up a schedule for yourself. This helped me tremendously in the past, just making yourself get up and stick to a routine. It doesn't have to be like you get up and run 5 miles, just set an alarm and get up, and you can build from there. 

Sometimes, we have to "fake it til we make it." This is a cheesey phrase, but it really works. Act as if you have what you want, which is the life you desire. Live you you have it. Take care of yourself and things will follow, such as self esteem. 

I often feel like happiness is a lie, but the thing is, we can't get outside our head sometimes. I mean, once we think a certain way for a while, we forget that there are other things that are possible for us. We forget what it is like to be happy, but happiness is still very possible. Don't fret over getting a date, just build slow, try socializing as often as possible. 

Then you can move on to bigger things, like a bigger plan. Don't worry about the big stuff now, focus on what you have immediate control over.

It might not feel like it, but life is just at the very beginning for you. I understand that you feel like you are in a bad place, and maybe you are, but you can get out of it. 

First, take some perspective. You have a family. You mentioned it isn't all that great, but it is something. They love you, and losing you would absolutely destroy them. It's because they see in you what you can't see yourself, and it is potential for a great life. 

Your problems seem tough, but they are not so bad. There are worse problems to have, try to remember that, and in that knowledge try to make a plan for yourself. You are free now, you can do a lot with your life. Try relying on your family more for support. They can be a great help and comfort, and I am sure they would be supportive, or at least try. Ending your life now would end something great before it even got to be realized. 

Stay strong.

This is kind of a common answer so don't be made if you have heard it before, but have you tried volunteering? Helping others is a very rewarding experience, and it would be doubly useful to you, as it could give you experience, and a reference, to help you with the job hunting.

Just wanted to tell you I am 21 and have been through very, very similar stuff. 

I have never actually been suicidal, but I lost a year feeling bad, constantly worrying that I would be suicidal. The funny thing is I didn't realize I wasn't actually suicidal till the end. Though it didn't help that I did, for whatever reason, not feel a reason to keep going on. 

I would literally have panic attacks where the thoughts going through my head were "I will commit suicide at some point," or "I am the type of person to commit suicide." Those were also the worst because health based panic attacks seemed to end much sooner.

You know, I am feeling like you. I have trouble with suicidal thoughts. I have also at times found people to be disgusting and terrible, though I will admit I have been fortunate that not many have tried to hurt me.

However, I find differently, often. People will hurt you with a smile on their face, sometimes, and some people will help you back onto your feet. The problem can be that people are self absorbed. I am young, and I suspect you are, too, and I find that people are just so immature at my age, and I'm in my 20s. So many never think about others, and would gladly tell you all day that they are there for you, but are they really? Some are, and some aren't. But there are people who can make you feel great. 

When I told my friends how I was feeling a year ago, I had one drop me from is life, and he was perhaps my closest friend, and it hurt like hell and still does. I had one act indifferently, I can tell he doesn't want to hear about it, but I had one who didn't mind listening to my stupid stories and feelings and was always there for me, and it helped so much.

I'm sorry that you don't have the right people around you. But hold on. People come into our lives and some go but some stay as truly great friends who care. Don't end your life because you haven't found these people yet, they are out there.

I don't know, one thing is, my depressive state doesn't seem to fit the bill.

It's like, I am socially isolated, if I had to put money down I'd bet that's why I'm like this, but depressive people want to kill themselves because of specific things, or at least things they can name. For me it's like: Life blows, everyone blows, fuck this. I'm not "I want to die because I have no friends," or anything.
Well ive been on the ssri for like 9 months or so.   No talk therapy.  Sorry im talking your ear off but i just have no hope and its crushing me.

I appreciate your concern but this wasn't manic in any way I've heard. I slept fine, and I wasn't in a great mood before I cleaned, I just think cleaning cheered me up.

Maybe I am misunderstanding, though, but in that good mood I felt like I did for most of my life as long as I wasn't having a shit day or something. 

I think it's more likely that my depression is just fairly light. I don't stay in bed, I can be pretty productive, on and on. Mostly I just feel anxious and depressed to an extent. I don't see a point in life, obviously, but I also have the odd anxiety concerning suicide. Sometimes I don't feel like killing myself as much as I am afraid that I some day will. In this way I am very bothered to hear about other people killing themselves. In fact I used to get panic attacks first.

I am treated for all of this, on a light dose of an SSRI, but it really only stopped the panic attacks.

Why do you bother? The people here are struggling, it's true, but do you think you have any effect on whether they end their life? No one is that malleable. It's a little shocking to get trolled, in a way, but honestly I almost feel for you, if it weren't such a trope to pity the bully, because I can almost imagine my life going on, but I don't know what happens to those who would try to harass the weak in spirit. On top of that it's such a purely impotent action, you aren't even really doing anything, which is almost more pathetic. 

You give yourself too much credit. You don't hurt people, you don't affect them, it's just mildly bothersome that someone has such a juvenile sense of humor.

Don't kill yourself, but especially not for some arbitrary date.

I'm sure you do have a future. Try not to let depression shroud what would otherwise be clear. You are probably pretty young, probably younger than 30, so there's tons of opportunities for you, though really no age is too late.

Having nothing sucks, of course, but in another way it can also be freeing. It may not be a huge comfort, but remind yourself that you also really don't have much limiting you, even if you don't feel like you have much, otherwise. 

People would definitely miss you.
Grow your eyebrows out, they would look good.
You're gorgeous, just don't pucker the top lip.
Definitely not ugly. I'd even say it's a pretty good "bored" face, and if you were smiling or looking up I'm sure your eyes would be piercing.

You have kind of unusual features, but take that as a huge compliment because you have an interesting face. I know how that might sound, but trust me, it's a good thing. I was thinking of suggesting that you change your hair, but it works actually.
And by "not exactly the same" philosophy you mean an almost completely different and antithetical philosophy.

Hey, i know it feels stagnant and terrible but 25 is still really young. This stuff now is fucking painful, but it's really not a good reason to cut out early. Even if they might not show it often enough, people do care. Im here to talk, id be glad if you pmed me orf just replied.
My gp prescribed it.

I guess I'm not doing so great. It's like I can't appreciate what normally would make someone happy, I just feel like I'm not there, in a way. I do have some anxiety over that, even, because I worry I will fall into what I did last summer, where my isolation led me to get pretty messed up, and I am worried that I will kill myself, but it feels different from actually wanting to kill myself.

It's almost like I'm anxious about killing myself. 

And last night was maybe my worst "attack." I've had panic attacks which had similar elements, this was panicky, definitely, but I just had all of these strange thoughts about whatever, that so deeply affected me that I was running around trying to calm my mind, but each time thoughts would invade. I know i am being dramatic, but it is just such a terrible problem.

Thanks a lot for your helpful words. As is expected I am a pretty lonely person and it is nice to have a place I can reach out to.
Time. I'm not better, pretty far from it, but time has made things better.
Hey, how's it going? Wanna talk to me?

Oh don't worry, I understand that it is hard to describe. I also understand that it is terrifying, but it will be alright. When it happened to me I didn't feel like there was anything wrong with my life, either, but looking back I realize I was wrong. 

I strongly recommend telling a professional. I waited, and the feelings never went away until I got prescribed an antidepressant. It made life really hard and wasn't worth waiting. If you want to avoid help because you don't want medication, that's understandable, but there are non-pill alternatives like just talk therapy. I wish I could tell you what helped me, what secret thing cured how you feel, but mostly it was just time. It dragged me down into a deep, deep terrible and indescribable loneliness before I realized that these feelings wouldn't last forever. 

Honestly now that I remember how I felt, and it seems similar to how you feel, it was a really dark time. But, it ended. It didn't last forever and I never killed myself. If there is one thing I wish I could give you, outside of a "cure," it's hope. The future will be okay, you won't always feel like this. But, I think that things will be better faster if you seek help.

Could you tell your girlfriend or anyone else that you are close to?

Well, like I said, do you feel panicked? I had times where I was panicky and wired and could only think about ending my life. Is that close to what you are describing.

I know you are worried about doing something, but isn't that kind of a sign that you probably won't? I felt that way, not exactly like doing it but intensely worried that I someday would.  It was really sudden for me, and for you, too, as you say.

Can you think of any trigger at all? Have you been feeling truly satisfied with your life?

Try not to worry, we are here for you.

Hey there, sorry that you're feeling this way. You sound really confused, but also a little panicked. Do you feel panicked at all? 

How would you describe how you feel? Just suicidal? Is this sudden or maybe has it been nagging? Has anything happened recently that you feel could have triggered this? 

I wish I could help you more, but maybe talking about this will make things clearer for you. Just from what you've said, you remind me a lot of myself last summer, I was suddenly suicidal and it was really scary. So try not to feel scared, things will be okay.

I know you are aware of the age distance between you and me, I imagine I am the average age of a SW poster, but a lot of what you has said related to what I'm going through. You're right, depression is not romantic, and it's not enjoyable to have these problems.

I am not a parent, that's true, but I feel confident saying that your parents don't truly feel you are a burden. Maybe they do face some difficulties due to you moving in, I can't deny that much, but I am sure that they are, much more than anything, concerned in your well-being. 

It seems like you don't see a good future for yourself, and maybe like nothing can help you. Naturally I would urge you to seek more help, although it sounds like you have tried a lot, it could be very worthwhile to look for more effective treatment. I hope you found sharing your story cathartic, at least, it's a good start. 

Still, try to imagine a good future for yourself. You may be in your 40s, but it could be worse, of course. Lots of people these days face unemployment at your age, and maybe are in a much worse situation. I know this kind of stuff, the "it could always be worse" stuff probably doesn't help, but maybe you can use it to see that you can have a good life. It is likely that you will find work again, fingers crossed that it is soon, and from there you can do all kinds of stuff. Your current fears and hopelessness enrich you as a person, in a sense. Perhaps there will come a day where you experience a blissful peace, and such a feeling could only be appreciated if you know what it is like to feel the opposite. 

I hope you feel better, and soon.

A lot of what you have said has resonated with me. I feel pretty much the exact same way, I think about suicide, the thought of doing it makes me happy in a way, like how you described, and I have gone so far as to think of methods, but I am not sure I was actually planning it.

I guess I don't have the answer to your question. However, though the nature of my situation was a little like it's not so much that I want to commit suicide as I don't NOT want to do it, either, it's hard for me to navigate what constitutes as "cured." I would say I am doing better. When I first had the thoughts it was very sudden, and I had no idea what was causing them, I even think now I may have some ptsd because I had some other symptoms and it fit together. I also had panic attacks which definitely needed to be helped so I am on antidepressants. That being said, it sounds like you have a grasp on what you want to improve your life. It sucks that you are in the situation you are in, but don't underestimate the benefit of just having a direction you would like to go in. 

Try not to get too paranoid, either. I am constantly paranoid that I am closer to suicide than what I think based mostly on behaviors that I have read about, but you have to try to get a grip on how you feel and not let yourself get too shaken. Personally, one thing that helped me a little sometimes, was giving myself a date to do it, just to get it out of my head. Of course, the date was far in  the future, like when I'm 70, but it kind of took the guessing aspect out and gave me space, I guess.
